approach: Add one reading-gate check, `check_speed_timeline(reading, request)`, in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, wired as one `step!(check_speed_timeline(reading, request));` line in `refusing_check` right after `check_outcome_state`. Cue detection runs over the request's OWN text only: `own_request_text` drops the lines Hestia quotes from records (title, `Failure class:`, `Cause:`, `Introspection … ; prevention it proposed:`) when the request is a root-cause request. The line prefixes are `pub(crate)` consts in reading.rs that `root_cause_request_at` in hestia.rs also uses, so they cannot drift (answers finding 2). Strong cues are faster, quicker, speedup, latency, `speed up`, `head start`, and a cut verb whose duration figure is its object (`save 12 minutes`, `cut 5 minutes from`) or follows `by`/`off` within five words, with no setting word (timeout, interval, ttl, retry, backoff …) between (finding 3). Weak cues (slow*, delay*, timing*) count only after a cut verb within five words (no setting word between) or after `too`. For a speed request the reading needs a `Timeline:` assumption naming a crates/ path, a `stages:` list of at least two stages each with a duration (unless it says no recorded timing), and a place word followed by a stage name. The fake reader gets one fixed Timeline so the drain test at drain.rs:7008 passes the real gate. A new athena-cli drain test pins that fake Timeline against both `check_speed_timeline` and `check_reading_references` in the fixture repo, so a change to ABSENCE_PHRASES fails a test that names the cause (finding 4). Root cause named everywhere: the reading stage checked a request's own figures only if the reader chose to, so readings were planned around stated timings with no stage timeline from the code. Fixed at the reading gate, which every speed request passes. The check judges the shape of the timeline, not whether its figures are true (stated in the doc comment and D163).

decisions.reason: Every reading passes `refusing_check`; the corpus test `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` forces a refusing case per step; no model call is needed; a refused reading gets one re-read with the refusal text. `check_outcome_state_doc_names_root_cause_and_scope` needs `check_outcome_state` right after `check_governance_coverage`, and a step after it leaves that position alone.

By then the reading is accepted and the criteria are fixed around the request's figure.
Runs after the producer built the wrong thing; the failure is in planning.

decisions.choice: Cue detection reads only the request's own text. `own_request_text(request)` returns the request without its quoted-record lines when the request is a root-cause request (some line starts with `ROOT_CAUSE_TITLE`, 'Fix the root cause of a repeated failure:'). It drops lines starting with that title, `CLASS_LINE` ('Failure class: '), `CAUSE_LINE` ('Cause: ') and `INTROSPECTION_LINE` ('Introspection ') containing `PREVENTION_MARK` ('; prevention it proposed:'). The consts are `pub(crate)` in reading.rs and `root_cause_request_at` (hestia.rs:458-507) formats with them.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2. Hestia builds every root-cause request by pasting cause and prevention text from earlier records (hestia.rs:466-489, title at :499 holds the first 100 characters of the cause). Those lines describe a rule to change, not a speed-up to make; this job's own request quotes 'claims a delay or speed-up' and would otherwise be refused as a speed request, with no truthful Timeline possible. Sharing the prefixes through consts means a change to the builder text is a compile-level change at one place. A request that is not root-cause-shaped is scanned whole, so a person's 'Cause: it is slow, make it faster' is still seen.

rejected.option: Scan the whole request and treat the quoted-cue root-cause request as a speed request (previous plan)
rejected.why: A false positive on a request shape Hestia generates automatically; it would make the reader invent a Timeline.

rejected.option: Duplicate the prefix strings in reading.rs
rejected.why: They drift from hestia.rs. One set of consts used by both is safer.

rejected.option: Skip any line starting with 'Cause:' in every request
rejected.why: Hides cues in a person's own request that happens to use the word.

decisions.choice: A cut verb is a strong cue only when the duration figure is its object or follows `by`/`off`: the figure (number plus unit) starts within two words after the verb (optionally after about, around, another, roughly, nearly, almost), or is directly preceded by `by` or `off` within five words after the verb. If a setting word (timeout, timeouts, interval, intervals, ttl, expiry, retention, lifetime, retry, backoff, debounce) sits between verb and figure, it is not a cue. Weak cues (slow, slower, slowest, slowly, slowdown, delay, delays, delayed, timing, timings) count only with a cut verb within five words before them with no setting word between, or with `too` right before. Strong stand-alone cues: faster, quicker, speedup, latency, `speed|speeds|sped|speeding` then `up`, `head start`.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3. 'Save the state every 30 seconds', 'Reduce the retry timeout to 10 s', 'Trim the log after 5 minutes' and 'Set the retry timeout to 10 s' put the figure after every/to/after, not as the object or after by/off, so they are not speed requests. 'Save 12 minutes', 'Cut 5 minutes from the checks', 'Reduce the check time by 5 minutes' and 'Shave 30 s off the run' are. Corpus accept pins cover each non-speed form. 'Reduce the retry delay' also stays out through the setting word. Cues are whole words over `request_words` (reading.rs:3503), which splits bullets, `1.`, `2)`, `(a)` parts and hyphens, so slowloris, speedometer, quickstart and timeline do not match.

rejected.option: Any cut verb with a figure within five words as a strong cue (previous plan)
rejected.why: Flags settings changes such as 'Save the state every 30 seconds'.

rejected.option: Bare delay, timing or slow as cues
rejected.why: Common in requests that are not about speed ('add a retry delay setting', 'fix a timing attack').

rejected.option: Substring match like the fake reader's SPEED_WORDS

decisions.choice: The Timeline must hold a crates/ path (`names_crates_path`, reading.rs:3838), a `stages:` clause with at least two ordered stages, a duration per stage (unless the Timeline says 'no recorded timing'), and a clause with a place word (sits, slowest, longest, bottleneck) followed by one of the stage names. The word 'delay' alone does not place the delay. 'No recorded timing' replaces only the durations, never the stages or the place.
decisions.reason: The three introspections ask for each stage in order, its measured duration and where the claimed delay sits. Stage order and place can be read from the code without run data; only the durations may be missing. The gate reads text only, so it checks the shape, not whether the figures are true; stated in the doc comment and D163.

risks.risk: False refusals: a request that uses a cut verb plus `by`/`off` and a figure for a non-speed purpose (for example 'Reduce the grace period by 5 minutes') is refused until the reader writes a Timeline.
risks.mitigation: Setting words (timeout, interval, ttl, retry, backoff …) and the object-of-verb rule keep the common settings forms out, pinned by accept cases. The reader gets one re-read with refusal text saying what to write, and can use the no-recorded-timing form. The declared 5% is an estimate, not measured.

risks.risk: The check judges the shape of the Timeline, not whether the figures are measured, so a reader can write invented numbers.
risks.mitigation: Stated as a limit in the doc comment and D163. The check still forces the crates/ path, the ordered stages and the stage where the delay sits into the reading before the criteria are fixed, which the three jobs lacked. Checking figures against run data is a named follow-up.

risks.risk: A target repository with no crates/ directory cannot meet the crates/ path rule.
risks.mitigation: Stated as a limit in D163. Athena's own repository is the target today; the rule mirrors `check_code_survey`.

risks.risk: The `stages:` grammar is stricter than free prose, so a reader may need the one re-read.
risks.mitigation: The refusal text and the seventh READING_RULES line give the form 'Timeline: read <crates/ path>; stages: <name> <duration>, <name> <duration>; the delay sits in <name>.' Corpus accept cases show it.

demonstrations.method: Run the refusal corpus. New cases give a speed request and a reading with no Timeline, and expect `Expected::Refuse("check_speed_timeline")`. Cases: 'speed-request-without-a-timeline' ('Move the call earlier to save 12 minutes.'); one per input form (dash bullet, star bullet, `1.` part, `2)` part, `(a)` part, retry complaint, quoted-record request with an own goal line); and the Timeline-defect refusals.
demonstrations.observes: `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome` passes, so each Refuse case is refused by `check_speed_timeline` and by no earlier check. `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` passes with the new step in the extracted list. `speed_timeline_refusal_is_declared_intended` passes. Input form to case id: dash bullet `speed-word-in-a-dash-bullet`; star bullet `speed-word-in-a-star-bullet`; `1.` part `speed-word-in-a-numbered-dot-part`; `2)` part `speed-word-in-a-numbered-paren-part`; `(a)` part `speed-word-in-a-lettered-paren-part`; retry complaint `retry-complaint-still-too-slow-without-a-timeline` (accept twin `...-with-a-timeline`); a request that cites a job without relying on it: existing `root-cause-request-cites-jobs…` cases at refusal_corpus.rs:604-617 stay Accept, and the new `root-cause-request-with-its-own-speed-goal-without-a-timeline` (Refuse) builds on the same shape with an own line 'Make the check faster.'; crate-relative path `timeline-with-a-crate-relative-path` (Refuse, names src/reading.rs); lookalike words `speed-word-lookalikes-are-not-speed-requests` (Accept); a brand word or environment variable is not read by this rule, so no case is added. Timeline-defect Refuse cases: `timeline-without-a-crates-path`, `timeline-with-one-stage-only`, `timeline-stage-without-a-duration`, `timeline-says-no-recorded-timing-without-stages`, `timeline-without-where-the-delay-sits`, `timeline-place-word-names-no-stage`, `timeline-label-not-at-the-start`. Each case is built from `base_reading()` with one field changed, so no earlier check refuses.
demonstrations.fails_without: Remove the `step!(check_speed_timeline(reading, request));` line and every Refuse("check_speed_timeline") case is accepted, so `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome` reports 'expected Refuse("check_speed_timeline"), got accepted'. Drop cue detection and the same cases fail. Drop the Timeline requirement and the defect cases fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `athena_core::reading::refusing_check` (reading.rs:3226, exists), called by `run(c)` in refusal_corpus.rs (exists). Fixture: `case()` and `base_reading()` (exist) with `repo_files()` injected as `Some(repo_files())` (exists). New cases come from `speed_timeline_cases()`, added by step 6. Guards: capability is Some and question is None. No double holds check logic.

demonstrations.method: The same corpus run holds accept cases: 'speed-request-with-a-timeline' (assumption 'Timeline: read crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs; stages: compile 9 min, check 40 s; the delay sits in compile.'); 'speed-request-timeline-says-no-recorded-timing' (stages named, no durations, place given); retry and root-cause-shaped requests with a Timeline; 'root-cause-request-quoting-speed-words-needs-no-timeline' (Hestia-shaped request whose title, Failure class, Cause and Introspection lines hold 'speed-up', 'faster' and 'cut 5 minutes', and whose own text has no cue; Accept); 'speed-request-question-reading-needs-no-timeline'; 'speed-word-lookalikes-are-not-speed-requests' ('Add a timeline view and a speedometer widget. Write a quickstart guide. Wait 30 seconds before the retry. Cover the slowloris case.'); and non-speed pins 'add-a-retry-delay-setting-is-not-a-speed-request', 'fix-a-timing-attack-is-not-a-speed-request', 'save-the-state-every-30-seconds-is-not-a-speed-request', 'set-the-retry-timeout-to-10-s-is-not-a-speed-request', 'reduce-the-retry-timeout-by-5-s-is-not-a-speed-request', 'trim-the-log-after-5-minutes-is-not-a-speed-request'. reading.rs unit tests `speed_requests_are_found_by_whole_word_cues_and_figures` and `a_timeline_assumption_needs_stages_durations_and_a_placed_delay` run the detector and the check directly (positives: 'Make the check faster', 'Speed up planning', 'a speed-up of the run', 'Cut 5 minutes from the checks', 'Save 12 minutes', 'Shave 30 s off the run', 'reduce the delay', 'still too slow'). A hestia.rs unit test feeds the real output of `root_cause_request` (cause, class and an introspection with prevention carrying speed words) through `crate::reading::speed_request` and expects false; a variant with an extra own line 'Make it faster.' expects true.
demonstrations.observes: All accept cases return None from `refusing_check`; the reading.rs and hestia.rs unit tests pass; the one-line errors start 'the reading was refused because'; the no-timing escape needs stages; skip when capability is None or a question is set.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the check refused every speed-word request regardless of the Timeline, 'speed-request-with-a-timeline' fails. If the detector scanned quoted record lines, the Hestia-shaped accept case and the hestia.rs test fail. If bare delay/timing or any cut verb plus a figure counted, the pins for retry delay, timing attack, 'Save the state every 30 seconds' and the retry timeout fail. If the check applied to non-speed requests, `steward-three-dash-bullets` fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `refusing_check` and, in unit tests, `check_speed_timeline` and `speed_request` (step 2 adds them); the hestia.rs test calls the real `root_cause_request` (hestia.rs:453, exists) with the `RepeatedCause`/`Records` builders used at hestia.rs:3381-3400 and 3609-3620 (exist). Fixtures: `case()`/`base_reading()` and `governed_reading` (reading.rs:7364, exist). The Timeline names only crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, which is in `repo_files()`, so `check_reading_references` does not refuse it.
